summary: Proceed, but do not dispatch until s3 (job 3bdec0e58d684c17) is harvested. Then build on s3's commit, not stage 2's, with s3's per-bucket variant (A, wait<0>; or B, double-buffered A) chosen for N16/N32. The s3 review found a register-A WAR hazard under wait<1> that is undefined behaviour in every instantiation, so stage 2's 'N16/N32 correct' and its 0.57x timing were measured on racy code. Clause (2), the 32-row cap, is a no-op for 8 <= T <= 32, which simplifies the change and lowers its risk.
justification: Design (kind: rewrite, stage 3 of the mid-M branch). The target is real. Marlin's pair is 95-114 / 170-176 / 156-207 us at bs=8/16/32, against floors of 37.3 / 52.5 / 70.8 us. These three shapes carry weight 180 of 360. The plan for evidence is good: a prepare gate per T bucket against master's exact path with cold L2, graph replays, interleaved A/B, p50 with a 3% margin, and an fp32-dequant reference with master's error printed beside it. Problems, in order of weight. (1) WEAKEST LINK: both pieces of evidence for N16/N32 come from stage-2 code that still has `wgmma_wait<1>()` in consume_item (s2 submission.py line ~724). The s3 review showed the next k-step's dequant rewrites a[] while the previous group may still read it. That is undefined behaviour in all <NB,G> instantiations, not only N64/N128, so stage 2 passing at N16/N32 may come from register allocation luck. Its prepare timing (0.57x Marlin) was also taken with the hazard present. If variant A turns out to be the fix, the wgmma pipeline loses its one-group overlap and the speed claim must be measured again. s3's per-bucket canary already times both variants at every bucket, N16/N32 included, with a cold-L2 pair time. That is the M2 evidence this hypothesis needs, and it arrives for free. (2) The 0.57x figure was measured at M=128/256 with all 32 experts hit and warm L2. At mid-M, about 7-14 local experts are touched with 1-4 rows each, and a 132-CTA persistent grid over 64 N-tiles x experts items gives roughly 1.7-3.5 waves, with tail imbalance and almost no reuse. The kernel is weight-bandwidth bound there, which is a different regime. (3) The mechanism claim 'Marlin's m-block scheme re-streams experts' does not hold at T <= 16. Every expert has at most 16 rows, so with block_size_m 16 Marlin already reads each expert once. Marlin's gap to the floor there is parallelism and dequant, not re-reads. (4) Counter-evidence: cuda-nvfp4-swapab-mma-persistent-small-m-inproc (0.925x) LOST on verify_1, decode_16 and decode_32, the same three shapes, with a persistent custom NVFP4 MMA. The per-bucket timing gate is what makes this attempt safe, so keep it strict. (5) Clause (2) is dead code in range. decode_item sets the bucket from nbk (16-row blocks): nbk <= 1 gives N16 and nbk <= 2 gives N32. A local expert can receive at most T <= 32 routes (top-8 experts are distinct per token), so nbk <= 2 always, and chunks are already cut every 8 blocks. ceil(cnt/32) is always 1. Implement it as a device assert or err-word bit (nbk > 2 means fall back), not as a new split path with extra capacity (T*8 + 32*31). That removes a new indexing surface. In practice this hypothesis is s2-fix-gate-from-8 restricted to 8..32 plus the timing gate, and that restriction is the correct way to make it distinct. (6) Milestone M3 needs <= 56/79/106 us. At ~1.5x the floor, that requires the persistent grid near HBM bandwidth with 7-14 experts, which is plausible only if the w13 item count fills 132 CTAs. Ask for the per-bucket achieved GB/s to be printed.
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (9080a71, master tip): it defines the incumbent at T <= 32 (w2 with use_atomic_add=True, use_fp32_reduce=False). Stage 2's _wg_time_vs_marlin and its Marlin reference calls predate it. After the rebase, the prepare gate must time master's own _moe_marlin, with the atomic kwargs, not stage 2's copy. Otherwise the 3% margin is measured against a w2 that is slower than the one the judge runs.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack (8440ae5): master's mid-M align is one _align_small_kernel launch (2.7-4.2 us). Stage 2's wgmma path calls SGLang's moe_align_block_size (plus the expert_map gather) at block 16. If that is kept at mid-M, the wgmma arm quietly drops a landed win, and the headline delta mixes kernel time with an align regression of several us. Feed the wgmma path from master's _align_small at block_size_m 16 (master self-checks it against moe_align_block_size), or count the align delta in the replaced-kernel sum.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m (192f225): at T < 32 the combine is master's Triton _post_norm_combine_kernel, which skips remote rows by slot id -1. The wgmma w2 epilogue scatters into cache3 by route. Unwritten local rows (cache3 is torch.empty) would be read. Stage 2's sentinel coverage check covered that only at M=128/256, so repeat it at T = 8/16/32.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / align-parallel-per-expert-verify: they act only at T >= 128 / T > 32. Disjoint from the gate, so no confound.
interference: No ab-revert or ab-tune companion. This is a rewrite gated per T bucket, so PATH CHOSEN = MARLIN reproduces master byte for byte and is the in-run control. The real attribution problem is the two siblings and s3. (a) Sequencing: wait for s3. s3 edits the same consume_item and wg_kernel source and decides per bucket between A and B. If cap32 is built now on stage 2, it runs the racy kernel and will then conflict with s3 on promotion. If s3 shows neither variant fixes N64/N128, the hazard is not the root cause, but s3's N16/N32 rows still give cap32's correctness and speed baseline. Either way, cap32 gets its base from s3's commit, and its per-bucket variant from s3's log. (b) The three siblings stay attributable this way. tiny-m-bucket16 (T <= 7, scored bs=1 only) is shape-disjoint from this run and w2-only-midm, so it can run in the same batch. midm-cap32 and w2-only-midm cover the same bs=8/16/32 shapes. Run them as two separate checks from the same s3-based base, never stacked on each other or on tiny-m. Each gets its own load_inline module name and a distinct PATH CHOSEN tag (e.g. 'WGMMA-PAIR' vs 'WGMMA-W2'). w2-only-midm is in effect this run's control: it isolates the w2 kernel against Marlin w2, and the remainder (cap32 minus w2-only, per shape) is the w13+silu contribution. That is the sub-change split a 'control' companion would give, so none is minted. Require cap32 to also print separate prepare timings for w13+silu and w2 (the judge profile merges Marlin's two launches and shows wg_kernel<...> rows by template). No promotion of any of the three before s3 is harvested and read.
rules_flags: None blocking. Bucket gating is by num_tokens (a shape), and the N16/N32 choice happens on device from align counts. No host branch on values, no .item() in kernel_fn. Keep all timing and self-check syncs in prepare(). Allocate scratch sized from T in prepare, or by shape only.

None of the 5 pre-timing tests (bs 4, 33, 257, 128-skewed, 1) falls in 8 <= T <= 32, so the wgmma mid-M path is first exercised on the scored shapes' per-call reference checks. A latent race (see justification 1) would fail the run there, not in tests. That is a further reason to build on s3's hazard-free variant.

Prepare budget: s2 took ~110-135 s. Adding s3's 16 instantiations, per-bucket canaries and >= 50-rep interleaved cold-L2 timing at three T buckets must stay under 300 s. Keep WG_SETUP_BUDGET_S and print the total.
open_questions: Which variant did s3 pick at N16 and N32, and what were its cold-L2 pair times there? If A (wait<0>) is the only passing variant, is the N16/N32 pair still under Marlin at M=128 single-expert? If not, the mid-M line has no M2 path, and cap32 should not be dispatched.

Does the build log (ptxas -Werror probe) report C7510 'wgmma serialized' for the N16/N32 instantiations under the real 168-register cap (__launch_bounds__(384,1))? Serialization would cap mid-M bandwidth.

At bs=8 / verify_1, how many local experts does the judge's routing touch (7 or fewer?), and does the w13 item count (64 N-tiles x experts) fill 132 CTAs with a reasonable tail? Print item counts and achieved GB/s per T bucket in prepare.

Should the synthetic routings for the prepare gate match the judge's load distributions (decode_16, decode_32, verify_1 skew)? A gate won on uniform-random routing may not transfer to the judged load.
Confirm that the rebase keeps master's _align_small (block 16) as the wgmma path's align at T <= 32, rather than reintroducing SGLang's moe_align_block_size.
